content:
maria: Heads up — canary split to 10% went out 90s ago. Noticed error spike in rerank path for model-x-3-small. Looking to abort the split and reconcile KV state quickly.

tom: on it. quick question — do we need a full disable or a traffic pin to primary? Metrics look noisy but 5xxs are real.

maria: Prefer fast abort to 0% (instant reroute) then follow with a safe disable for the canary instances to avoid flapping. We also need to clear any prefix-based KV entries used by the canary to avoid stale cache hits.

kevin: Agreed. Plan: 1) set traffic-split canary=0 2) drain existing canary sessions 3) run prefix sweep for kv://canary/model-x-3-small/* 4) safe-disable canary fleet in console.

anya: small nit — draining takes time because SDK clients have sticky routing for 30s TTL. We should reduce session-ttl for the canary service before we flip to minimize stragglers. I can patch the route config if we act fast.

maria: do it. Patch the route to session_ttl=5s for canary. then flip.

anya: patch deployed: session_ttl=5s for route model-x-canary.

deploy-bot: command accepted: set-traffic --route model-x --variant canary --percent 0

kevin: flip issued. should be immediate for new requests. old sessions will drain over the next ~10s.

maria: while draining, run a KV reconciliation scan to capture keys written during the canary window. We want to copy relevant KV into a holding namespace and then delete canary-only keys. Any objections?

tom: fine. pattern to sweep? we use prefix kv://model-x/canary/<request_id>. Also remember rate limits on kv-scan; use pagination.

kevin: using the bulk-scan job with --rate 200 qps. command: ```./tools/kv-scan --prefix model-x/canary/ --rate 200 --out /tmp/canary-keys.json``` then ```./tools/kv-delete --file /tmp/canary-keys.json --dry-run``` run dry-run first.

anya: important: telemetry lag. The dashboard ingest for per-route errors takes ~45s to update. Don't overreact before 2m. Also set the rollback annotation on the deployment for audit.

maria: noted. I've added annotation: rollback_reason=auto-observed-5xx. Also creating a console ticket for follow-up.

sre-bot: alert suppressed for route model-x: reason=manual-abort-in-progress user=maria

kevin: dry-run complete — 432 keys identified. pushing delete now. ```./tools/kv-delete --file /tmp/canary-keys.json```

tom: delete done. confirming no canary-specific TTLs left. run a quick healthcheck: ```curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.internal/model-x/health | jq .routes```

maria: healthcheck shows primary healthy, error rate back to baseline after drain. Rolling safe-disable on canary fleet: console -> disable with reason "abort due to 5xx regression"

deploy-bot: disable-fleet acknowledged: fleet=model-x-canary initiated by maria

anya: follow-up checklist: 1) postmortem probe on why cache keys were written differently, 2) add preflight to run kv-scan simulation in staging for next rollout, 3) add metric for canary-kv-write-rate.

kevin: I'll open an eng-platform task for preflight simulation and add a console toggle to auto-reconcile KV on abort.

maria: thanks team — nice quick coordination. Let's hold off on re-deploy until we have the preflight and the metric in place. :thumbsup:
